tasks.subject: B6: ScheduleConfig + UiSettings replace Namespace threading
tasks.description:
**Goal:** One frozen ScheduleConfig dataclass, constructed by both scout_schedule_cli.parse_args() and ui/server.py's schedule-download worker, replaces the argparse Namespace both sites build today. email_report gets an explicit default everywhere, removing the getattr(args, "email_report", False) defense in async_main. UiSettings (currently inline in ui/server.py) also moves into scoutmb.config, since a new sibling module wouldn't fit the spec's dependency-edge table.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/config.py`
- Modify: `scout_schedule_cli.py`, `ui/server.py`, `tests/unit/test_ui_settings.py` (import fix)
- Test: `tests/unit/test_config.py`, `tests/contracts/test_cli_defaults_parity.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ScheduleConfig's dataclass field defaults and parse_args()'s argparse defaults are the same 13 values, sourced from one place
- [ ] parse_args() returns a ScheduleConfig, not an argparse.Namespace
- [ ] ui/server.py's schedule-download worker constructs ScheduleConfig with email_report=False explicit
- [ ] getattr(config, "email_report", False) no longer appears in async_main
- [ ] tests/characterization/test_cli_sched_matrix.py passes unmodified
- [ ] UiSettings importable from scoutmb.config; ui/server.py's own class becomes a re-export; test_ui_settings.py's import updated

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_config.py tests/contracts/test_cli_defaults_parity.py tests/characterization/test_cli_sched_matrix.py tests/unit/test_ui_settings.py -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX: UiSettings placement added to this task (was going to live in a new scoutmb.ui_settings module in sub-plan 3, which the dependency-edge table doesn't recognize as a layer). See plan doc Task B6.

tasks.subject: B7.1: core/run_state.py versioned run-state machine
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A total transition table over RunState/RunEvent: every (state, event) pair either transitions or raises IllegalTransition, proven by a Hypothesis property AND an exhaustive parametrized test pinning the exact intended shape of the table.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/core/run_state.py`
- Test: `tests/unit/jobs/test_run_state.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] RunStateMachine().apply(RunEvent.START) transitions IDLE -> RUNNING
- [ ] Every explicitly-illegal edge raises IllegalTransition and leaves .state unchanged
- [ ] A Hypothesis property over the full RunState x RunEvent Cartesian product proves totality
- [ ] An exhaustive parametrized test over every (state, event) pair asserts the EXACT expected next-state (or IllegalTransition) -- the Hypothesis property alone only proves totality, not that the table has the right shape
- [ ] No terminal state (COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED) has any legal outgoing transition

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/unit/jobs/test_run_state.py -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX: added the exhaustive parametrized test -- the Hypothesis property alone would pass for any total-but-wrong transition table. See plan doc Task B7.1.

tasks.subject: B7.2: runtime/jobs.py lifespan-owned JobSupervisor (duplicate-ID safe)
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A JobSupervisor that retains a reference to every asyncio.Task it starts (fixing the GC hazard in ui/server.py's unreferenced asyncio.create_task(worker()) calls) and, on shutdown(), cancels and awaits all of them, including asyncio.to_thread work. Safe against job-ID reuse: an older task's completion never evicts a newer task's still-live registry entry.

**Files:**
- Create: `src/scoutmb/runtime/__init__.py`, `src/scoutmb/runtime/jobs.py`
- Test: `tests/integration/test_job_supervisor.py`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A started task is retained until it finishes, then auto-removed via add_done_callback
- [ ] shutdown() cancels every running task and awaits all of them; registry empty and no pending task afterward
- [ ] Cancelling a task awaiting asyncio.to_thread still leaves bookkeeping clean -- precise claim, does not claim the underlying thread stopped
- [ ] shutdown() is idempotent
- [ ] Reusing a job_id before its predecessor finishes does not lose the newer task's registry entry when the predecessor later completes
- [ ] Uses asyncio.create_task, not asyncio.ensure_future (start()'s parameter is always a Coroutine, never an existing Future/Task)

**Verify:** `uv run pytest tests/integration/test_job_supervisor.py -q` → PASS

POST-CODEX FIX: fixed a real bug where an unconditional done-callback pop could evict a newer task sharing a reused job_id; switched ensure_future to create_task. See plan doc Task B7.2.
